title.value: Auto-reply to WooCommerce customer emails with order lookups

introduction.value: A self-hosted OpenClaw agent answers incoming store emails by looking up order details, and can email confirmations to customers with orders still processing.

method.value: OpenClaw runs on a VPS with the WordPress and WooClaw-Lite skills, which give it check_order, find_product and store_status. An Agentmail inbox sends a webhook for each incoming email. A system prompt tells the agent to look up the order and reply in the thread, and to acknowledge refunds and complaints and flag them for a human. A manual mode handles batch confirmations.

outcome.value: The source's example is a shipping-status email that gets a reply with tracking and delivery details. The batch prompt for processing orders is said to replace 20-30 minutes of dashboard work. It reports no measured results from a real store.

notes.value: Use a dedicated WordPress user with limited permissions, and a webhook token so only Agentmail can trigger the agent. The VPS needs Docker and at least 2 GB RAM.

source_text.body:
Auto-reply to WooCommerce customer emails with order lookups
A self-hosted OpenClaw agent answers incoming store emails by looking up order details, and can email confirmations to customers with orders still processing.
Done with
OC
OpenClaw
What they did
OpenClaw runs on a VPS with the WordPress and WooClaw-Lite skills, which give it check_order, find_product and store_status. An Agentmail inbox sends a webhook for each incoming email. A system prompt tells the agent to look up the order and reply in the thread, and to acknowledge refunds and complaints and flag them for a human. A manual mode handles batch confirmations.
How it went
The source's example is a shipping-status email that gets a reply with tracking and delivery details. The batch prompt for processing orders is said to replace 20-30 minutes of dashboard work. It reports no measured results from a real store.
Worth knowing
Use a dedicated WordPress user with limited permissions, and a webhook token so only Agentmail can trigger the agent. The VPS needs Docker and at least 2 GB RAM.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
Watch the inbox at [store support email address] for new customer emails about [WooCommerce store name]. For each one, look up the customer's order in WooCommerce using [order number or customer email], then draft a reply with the real order status and details. Save every draft for my review and show me the drafts; do not send any email, including confirmations to customers whose orders are still processing, until I approve it. Stop once all emails from the last [number] days have a draft.
Original source: https://www.hostinger.com/tutorials/how-to-automate-woocommerce-customer-email-replies-with-openclaw/
